# @plurid/aptuitive-react

<!-- Generated by `pnpm docs` from packages/react/src: edit the JSDoc there. -->

React bindings: the provider, hooks, the page renderer and the generic blocks, drawn with a kit you map to your design system. React 18.3 or 19.

Install: `pnpm add @plurid/aptuitive-react`, with `react` ^18.3.0 || ^19.0.0, `zod` ^4.2.0 as peers. Guides: [React](../react.md), [Pages](../pages.md).

- [The provider](#the-provider): [`AptBanner`](#aptbanner), [`AptDebug`](#aptdebug), [`AptuitiveContext`](#aptuitivecontext), [`AptuitiveProvider`](#aptuitiveprovider), [`AptYourInterface`](#aptyourinterface), [`Confirmations`](#confirmations), [`useAptuitive`](#useaptuitive), [`AptuitiveContextValue`](#aptuitivecontextvalue), [`ElementProps`](#elementprops), [`ProviderProps`](#providerprops)
- [Hooks](#hooks): [`useAction`](#useaction), [`useAptuitiveRouter`](#useaptuitiverouter), [`useCommand`](#usecommand), [`useConfirmation`](#useconfirmation), [`useLatest`](#uselatest), [`useLifecycle`](#uselifecycle), [`useLocation`](#uselocation), [`usePending`](#usepending), [`usePerform`](#useperform), [`usePlan`](#useplan), [`useQueries`](#usequeries), [`useQuery`](#usequery), [`useRanked`](#useranked), [`useSnapshot`](#usesnapshot), [`useStandard`](#usestandard), [`useSurface`](#usesurface), [`useUserPages`](#useuserpages), [`useView`](#useview), [`Request`](#request)
- [Rendering pages](#rendering-pages): [`GenericBlock`](#genericblock), [`Page`](#page), [`BlockComponents`](#blockcomponents), [`BlockProps`](#blockprops), [`PageProps`](#pageprops), [`RegionComponents`](#regioncomponents)

## The provider

Source: [`provider.tsx`](../../packages/react/src/provider.tsx)

### AptBanner

`<apt-banner>`: what just changed and why, with Revert and Keep. It floats at the bottom right;
`docked` puts it in the page's flow.

```ts
function AptBanner(
  props: HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement> & {
    client: unknown;
  } & {
    docked?: boolean;
  },
): ReactElement;
```

### AptDebug

`<apt-debug>`: the developer panel.

```ts
function AptDebug(
  props: HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement> & {
    client: unknown;
  } & {
    personas?: readonly Persona[];
  },
): ReactElement;
```

### AptuitiveContext

The provider's context; `useAptuitive` reads it.

```ts
const AptuitiveContext: Context<AptuitiveContextValue | undefined>;
```

Uses: [`AptuitiveContextValue`](#aptuitivecontextvalue).

### AptuitiveProvider

Makes a client and a kit available to pages, generic blocks and confirmations below it, and
connects the page's lifecycle (see `useLifecycle`).

```ts
function AptuitiveProvider<C extends AnyContract>(props: ProviderProps<C>): JSX.Element;
```

Uses: [`AnyContract`](core.md#anycontract), [`ProviderProps`](#providerprops).

### AptYourInterface

`<apt-your-interface>`: the user's definition, readable and revertible.

```ts
function AptYourInterface(props: ElementProps): ReactElement;
```

Uses: [`ElementProps`](#elementprops).

### Confirmations

Asks the user before a generated interface changes data: the action, what it will do it to,
and for destructive actions the phrase to type. Mount it once, inside the provider; without
it, generated interfaces can't write at all.

```ts
function Confirmations(): JSX.Element | null;
```

### useAptuitive

The client and kit from the nearest provider.

```ts
function useAptuitive(): AptuitiveContextValue;
```

Uses: [`AptuitiveContextValue`](#aptuitivecontextvalue).

### AptuitiveContextValue

What the provider shares below it: the client, and the kit generic blocks draw with.

Uses: [`Aptuitive`](core.md#aptuitive), [`Kit`](#kit).

| Property | Type        | Description                                    |
| -------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `client` | `Aptuitive` | The client pages, hooks and confirmations use. |
| `kit`    | `Kit`       | The kit generic blocks draw with.              |

### ElementProps

What the meta-interface wrappers take: HTML attributes, and the client the element shows.

```ts
type ElementProps = HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement> & {
  client: unknown;
};
```

### ProviderProps

What `AptuitiveProvider` takes: the client, and the kit generic blocks draw with.

Uses: [`AnyContract`](core.md#anycontract), [`Aptuitive`](core.md#aptuitive), [`Kit`](#kit).

Type parameters: `C extends AnyContract`.

| Property    | Type           | Default      | Description                                                                 |
| ----------- | -------------- | ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `client`    | `Aptuitive<C>` |              | The client from `createAptuitive`.                                          |
| `kit?`      | `Kit`          | `defaultKit` | What generic blocks are drawn with.                                         |
| `styles?`   | `boolean`      | `true`       | Adds the default kit's styles, which kits built with `createKit` still use. |
| `children?` | `ReactNode`    |              | The application.                                                            |

## Hooks

Source: [`hooks.ts`](../../packages/react/src/hooks.ts)

### useAction

The application's own control for an action: running it records usage (no hand-written
`record()`), and the application confirms in its own way.

```ts
function useAction<C extends AnyContract, A extends ActionIdOf<C>>(
  client: Aptuitive<C>,
  action: A,
): (params?: ParamsOf<C, A>, options?: Omit<PerformOptions, 'origin'>) => Promise<PerformResult>;
```

Uses: [`ActionIdOf`](core.md#actionidof), [`AnyContract`](core.md#anycontract), [`Aptuitive`](core.md#aptuitive), [`ParamsOf`](core.md#paramsof), [`PerformOptions`](core.md#performoptions), [`PerformResult`](core.md#performresult).

### useAptuitiveRouter

Connects any router: tells the client every route change and lets it follow links through
the router. With React Router, `useAptuitiveRouter(client, { path: pathname + search,
navigate })`; with Next.js, `{ path: usePathname(), navigate: useRouter().push }`.

```ts
function useAptuitiveRouter<C extends AnyContract>(
  client: Aptuitive<C>,
  router: {
    path: string;
    navigate: (href: string) => void;
  },
): void;
```

Uses: [`AnyContract`](core.md#anycontract), [`Aptuitive`](core.md#aptuitive).

### useCommand

Asks in the user's own words, tracking the request for the interface.

```ts
function useCommand<C extends AnyContract>(
  client: Aptuitive<C>,
): {
  ask: (
    text: string,
    options?: {
      goal?: boolean;
    },
  ) => Promise<Adaptation>;
  pending: boolean;
  result: Adaptation | undefined;
  error: unknown;
};
```

Uses: [`Adaptation`](core.md#adaptation), [`AnyContract`](core.md#anycontract), [`Aptuitive`](core.md#aptuitive).

### useConfirmation

The run waiting for the user's yes, with the means to answer it.

```ts
function useConfirmation<C extends AnyContract>(
  client: Aptuitive<C>,
): {
  confirmation: Confirmation | undefined;
  confirm: (phrase?: string) => boolean;
  cancel: () => void;
};
```

Uses: [`AnyContract`](core.md#anycontract), [`Aptuitive`](core.md#aptuitive), [`Confirmation`](core.md#confirmation).

### useLatest

The latest adaptation, for banners. Re-renders only when a new one arrives.

```ts
function useLatest<C extends AnyContract>(client: Aptuitive<C>): Adaptation | undefined;
```

Uses: [`Adaptation`](core.md#adaptation), [`AnyContract`](core.md#anycontract), [`Aptuitive`](core.md#aptuitive).

### useLifecycle

Connects the page's lifecycle to sessions: coming back to a tab after an idle gap applies
pending changes before the user acts, each session is planned from use once (see `learn`), and
leaving the page writes state to storage. Starts no sessions itself and plans a session only
once, so React's development double-mounting changes nothing. `AptuitiveProvider` calls it;
call it yourself only for a client used without the provider.

```ts
function useLifecycle<C extends AnyContract>(client: Aptuitive<C>): void;
```

Uses: [`AnyContract`](core.md#anycontract), [`Aptuitive`](core.md#aptuitive).

### useLocation

Where the user is, as the router last reported it.

```ts
function useLocation<C extends AnyContract>(client: Aptuitive<C>): Location | undefined;
```

Uses: [`AnyContract`](core.md#anycontract), [`Aptuitive`](core.md#aptuitive), [`Location`](core.md#location).

### usePending

Changes waiting for the next safe moment.

```ts
function usePending<C extends AnyContract>(client: Aptuitive<C>): readonly Pending[];
```

Uses: [`AnyContract`](core.md#anycontract), [`Aptuitive`](core.md#aptuitive), [`Pending`](core.md#pending).

### usePerform

Runs actions; writes from generated interfaces wait for the user's yes.

```ts
function usePerform<C extends AnyContract>(
  client: Aptuitive<C>,
): <A extends ActionIdOf<C>>(
  action: A,
  params?: ParamsOf<C, A>,
  options?: PerformOptions,
) => Promise<PerformResult>;
```

Uses: [`AnyContract`](core.md#anycontract), [`Aptuitive`](core.md#aptuitive), [`ParamsOf`](core.md#paramsof), [`PerformOptions`](core.md#performoptions), [`PerformResult`](core.md#performresult).

### usePlan

Plans on request, tracking it for the interface.

```ts
function usePlan<C extends AnyContract>(
  client: Aptuitive<C>,
): {
  plan: () => Promise<Adaptation>;
  pending: boolean;
  result: Adaptation | undefined;
  error: unknown;
};
```

Uses: [`Adaptation`](core.md#adaptation), [`AnyContract`](core.md#anycontract), [`Aptuitive`](core.md#aptuitive).

### useQueries

Several queries' results at once, in order; an undefined query reads as loading.

```ts
function useQueries<C extends AnyContract>(
  client: Aptuitive<C>,
  queries: readonly (Query | undefined)[],
  scope?: DataScope,
): readonly DataEntry[];
```

Uses: [`AnyContract`](core.md#anycontract), [`Aptuitive`](core.md#aptuitive), [`DataEntry`](core.md#dataentry), [`DataScope`](core.md#datascope), [`Query`](core.md#query-type).

### useQuery

One query's result, shared with everything else that asks for it. Fetches when there is none
or it went stale; renders from the cache meanwhile.

```ts
function useQuery<C extends AnyContract>(
  client: Aptuitive<C>,
  query: Query | undefined,
  scope?: DataScope,
): DataEntry;
```

Uses: [`AnyContract`](core.md#anycontract), [`Aptuitive`](core.md#aptuitive), [`DataEntry`](core.md#dataentry), [`DataScope`](core.md#datascope), [`Query`](core.md#query-type).

### useRanked

Every action, ranked for a palette by how the user reaches for them.

```ts
function useRanked<C extends AnyContract>(
  client: Aptuitive<C>,
): readonly ActionView<ActionIdOf<C>>[];
```

Uses: [`ActionIdOf`](core.md#actionidof), [`ActionView`](core.md#actionview), [`AnyContract`](core.md#anycontract), [`Aptuitive`](core.md#aptuitive).

### useSnapshot

The client's whole snapshot. It changes with every usage event, so use it for panels, not for
the interface itself; prefer [`useSurface`](#usesurface) there.

```ts
function useSnapshot<C extends AnyContract>(client: Aptuitive<C>): Snapshot;
```

Uses: [`AnyContract`](core.md#anycontract), [`Aptuitive`](core.md#aptuitive), [`Snapshot`](core.md#snapshot).

### useStandard

A surface as the application ships it, whatever the user's definition.

```ts
function useStandard<C extends AnyContract, K extends SurfaceIdOf<C>>(
  client: Aptuitive<C>,
  id: K,
  context?: string,
): SurfaceValueOf<C, K>;
```

Uses: [`AnyContract`](core.md#anycontract), [`Aptuitive`](core.md#aptuitive), [`SurfaceIdOf`](core.md#surfaceidof), [`SurfaceValueOf`](core.md#surfacevalueof).

### useSurface

A surface's value, for the current context unless one is given. Re-renders only when that
value changes. Server rendering uses the standard layout, so hydration never mismatches; the
user's definition follows on the client.

```ts
function useSurface<C extends AnyContract, K extends SurfaceIdOf<C>>(
  client: Aptuitive<C>,
  id: K,
  context?: string,
): SurfaceValueOf<C, K>;
```

Uses: [`AnyContract`](core.md#anycontract), [`Aptuitive`](core.md#aptuitive), [`SurfaceIdOf`](core.md#surfaceidof), [`SurfaceValueOf`](core.md#surfacevalueof).

### useUserPages

The pages the user made.

```ts
function useUserPages<C extends AnyContract>(client: Aptuitive<C>): readonly UserPage[];
```

Uses: [`AnyContract`](core.md#anycontract), [`Aptuitive`](core.md#aptuitive), [`UserPage`](core.md#userpage).

### useView

Whether the user is looking at their own interface or the standard one.

```ts
function useView<C extends AnyContract>(client: Aptuitive<C>): View;
```

Uses: [`AnyContract`](core.md#anycontract), [`Aptuitive`](core.md#aptuitive), [`View`](core.md#view).

### Request

A request's state, for an interface: whether it is in flight, and its result or error.

Type parameters: `T`.

| Property  | Type             | Description                             |
| --------- | ---------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `pending` | `boolean`        | Whether a request is in flight.         |
| `result`  | `T \| undefined` | The last result, once there is one.     |
| `error`   | `unknown`        | Why the last request failed, if it did. |

## Rendering pages

Source: [`generic.tsx`](../../packages/react/src/generic.tsx), [`page.tsx`](../../packages/react/src/page.tsx)

### GenericBlock

Draws one generic block from its props, its page's queries and the kit.

```ts
function GenericBlock(props: {
  element: Element;
  page: AnyPage;
  current?: string;
}): JSX.Element | null;
```

Uses: [`AnyPage`](core.md#anypage), [`Element`](core.md#element).

### Page

Renders a page, standard or redesigned, with the application's own components. Sections,
tabs and blocks carry `data-layout`, `data-block` and `data-element` attributes for styling.

```ts
function Page<B extends Record<string, BlockSpec>>(props: PageProps<B>): JSX.Element | null;
```

Uses: [`BlockSpec`](core.md#blockspec), [`PageProps`](#pageprops).

### BlockComponents

One component per block of a page; the types come from the contract's block schemas.

```ts
type BlockComponents<B extends Record<string, BlockSpec>> = {
  [K in Extract<keyof B, string>]: ComponentType<BlockProps<PropsOf<B[K]>>>;
};
```

Uses: [`BlockProps`](#blockprops), [`BlockSpec`](core.md#blockspec), [`PropsOf`](core.md#propsof).

### BlockProps

Props every block component receives: its own typed props, and the page's context value.

Type parameters: `P`.

| Property  | Type                  | Description                                          |
| --------- | --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `props`   | `P`                   | The block's props, checked against its schema.       |
| `context` | `string \| undefined` | The page's context value, such as the service shown. |

### PageProps

What `Page` takes: the page to draw, the components for the application's blocks and regions, and
the row it is about.

Uses: [`AnyPage`](core.md#anypage), [`BlockComponents`](#blockcomponents), [`BlockSpec`](core.md#blockspec), [`RegionComponents`](#regioncomponents).

Type parameters: `B extends Record<string, BlockSpec>`.

| Property     | Type                 | Default                       | Description                                                                     |
| ------------ | -------------------- | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`      | `AnyPage`            |                               | The page, usually from `useSurface`.                                            |
| `blocks`     | `BlockComponents<B>` |                               | A component for each of the application's own blocks; generic blocks need none. |
| `regions?`   | `RegionComponents`   |                               | What each region shows, such as the page as it was before Aptuitive.            |
| `context?`   | `string`             |                               | The page's context value, such as the service shown.                            |
| `current?`   | `string`             | the row the location is about | The key of the row the page is about.                                           |
| `className?` | `string`             | `'apt-page'`                  | The class of the page's wrapper.                                                |

### RegionComponents

Components for the contract's regions: parts of the application as it already is.

```ts
type RegionComponents = Readonly<
  Record<
    string,
    ComponentType<{
      context: string | undefined;
    }>
  >
>;
```

## The kit

Source: [`kit.tsx`](../../packages/react/src/kit.tsx)

### createKit

A kit with some primitives replaced, and some value types drawn differently: start from the
default and swap in the design system's parts as they are mapped.

```ts
function createKit(
  overrides?: Partial<Kit> & {
    values?: ValueRenderers;
  },
): Kit;
```

Uses: [`Kit`](#kit), [`ValueRenderers`](#valuerenderers).

### defaultKit

Semantic HTML with `apt-*` classes, themed through `--apt-*` custom properties.

```ts
const defaultKit: Kit;
```

Uses: [`Kit`](#kit).

### kitStyles

The default kit's styles, as a string: for a `<style>`, or a shadow root.

```ts
const kitStyles: string;
```

### ChartPoint

One point of a chart series.

| Property | Type               | Description                            |
| -------- | ------------------ | -------------------------------------- |
| `x`      | `number \| string` | A time in milliseconds, or a category. |
| `label`  | `string`           | The point's label, as people read it.  |
| `y`      | `number`           | Its value.                             |

### ChartSeries

One series of a kit `Chart`, such as one value of a split.

Uses: [`ChartPoint`](#chartpoint).

| Property | Type                    | Description                       |
| -------- | ----------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `name`   | `string`                | The series' name, for its legend. |
| `points` | `readonly ChartPoint[]` | Its points, in order.             |

### Kit

The presentational parts every generic block is drawn with. Map them to a design system once,
one at a time if need be, and Aptuitive's blocks look native.

```ts
interface Kit {
  Stack: ComponentType<{
    children?: ReactNode;
  }>;
  Title: ComponentType<{
    children?: ReactNode;
  }>;
  Section: ComponentType<{
    title: string;
    layout: 'stack' | 'grid' | 'columns';
    depth: number;
    count: number;
    children?: ReactNode;
  }>;
  Grid: ComponentType<{
    children?: ReactNode;
    columns?: number;
  }>;
  Card: ComponentType<{
    title?: string;
    children?: ReactNode;
  }>;
  Tabs: ComponentType<{
    label?: string;
    tabs: readonly {
      id: string;
      title: string;
      content: ReactNode;
    }[];
  }>;
  Text: ComponentType<{
    children?: ReactNode;
    tone?: 'muted' | 'strong';
  }>;
  Table: ComponentType<{
    columns: readonly TableColumn[];
    rows: readonly TableRow[];
    density?: 'comfortable' | 'compact';
    caption?: string;
  }>;
  List: ComponentType<{
    items: readonly ListItem[];
  }>;
  Stat: ComponentType<{
    label: string;
    value: ReactNode;
    change?: number;
    partial?: boolean;
  }>;
  Chart: ComponentType<{
    kind: 'line' | 'bar' | 'area' | 'pie';
    series: readonly ChartSeries[];
    stacked?: boolean;
    label?: string;
  }>;
  Badge: ComponentType<{
    children?: ReactNode;
    tone?: 'neutral' | 'good' | 'warning' | 'bad';
  }>;
  Value: ComponentType<ValueProps>;
  Button: ComponentType<{
    children?: ReactNode;
    onClick?: () => void;
    tone?: 'primary' | 'plain' | 'danger';
    size?: 'small' | 'regular' | 'large';
    disabled?: boolean;
    type?: 'button' | 'submit';
  }>;
  Link: ComponentType<{
    href: string;
    children?: ReactNode;
    onClick?: () => void;
  }>;
  Field: ComponentType<{
    field: Field;
    value: string;
    onChange: (value: string) => void;
    label?: string;
    required?: boolean;
  }>;
  Dialog: ComponentType<{
    title: string;
    children?: ReactNode;
    onClose: () => void;
  }>;
  Notice: ComponentType<{
    tone: 'success' | 'error';
    children?: ReactNode;
  }>;
  Status: ComponentType<{
    state: 'empty' | 'loading' | 'error' | 'partial';
    message?: string;
  }>;
}
```

Uses: [`ChartSeries`](#chartseries), [`Field`](core.md#field-type), [`ListItem`](#listitem), [`TableColumn`](#tablecolumn), [`TableRow`](#tablerow), [`ValueProps`](#valueprops).

| Property  | Description                                                                                                                                                                              |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Stack`   | Parts one above another, such as a form's fields and its button.                                                                                                                         |
| `Title`   | A page's title, from its root section; the page's own heading.                                                                                                                           |
| `Section` | A page's section: its title, and its blocks laid out as a stack, a grid or columns. Map it to the design system's container and heading; `depth` is 1 for a page's top-level sections.   |
| `Grid`    | Parts side by side in columns, such as a detail block's fields or a board's columns.                                                                                                     |
| `Card`    | A framed part with an optional title, such as a note or a board's column.                                                                                                                |
| `Tabs`    | A section whose children show one at a time, each under its tab.                                                                                                                         |
| `Text`    | A run of text, plain, muted or strong.                                                                                                                                                   |
| `Table`   | Rows under column headers: the table block, with row actions in its cells.                                                                                                               |
| `List`    | Rows as a list, each with a title, a subtitle, a badge and its own actions.                                                                                                              |
| `Stat`    | One figure with its label: the metric block.                                                                                                                                             |
| `Chart`   | Series drawn as lines, bars, areas or a pie.                                                                                                                                             |
| `Badge`   | A short label with a tone, such as a status.                                                                                                                                             |
| `Value`   | One value, shown by its type, such as money with its currency or a reference by name.                                                                                                    |
| `Button`  | A button: row actions, the actions block and dialogs use it.                                                                                                                             |
| `Link`    | A link to a route, followed through the application's router.                                                                                                                            |
| `Field`   | A labelled input for one field, such as an action's param in a form.                                                                                                                     |
| `Dialog`  | A modal with a title, for confirmations and the forms of actions run from a row.                                                                                                         |
| `Notice`  | What happened when an action ran from a generated page. Map it to the design system's toast or alert: each run mounts a new one, so a toast can show itself on mount and render nothing. |
| `Status`  | What a block shows around or instead of data: no rows, loading, an error, or a partial result.                                                                                           |

### ListItem

One item of a kit `List`: a title, optional details and a badge, its actions, and how to open it.

| Property    | Type         | Description                                |
| ----------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------ |
| `key`       | `string`     | The item's key, for React and for actions. |
| `title`     | `ReactNode`  | What the item is called.                   |
| `subtitle?` | `ReactNode`  | A second line.                             |
| `meta?`     | `ReactNode`  | A detail beside the item, such as a time.  |
| `badge?`    | `ReactNode`  | A badge, such as a status.                 |
| `actions?`  | `ReactNode`  | Buttons for the item's actions.            |
| `onOpen?`   | `() => void` | Opens the item's own page.                 |

### TableColumn

One column of a kit `Table`: the key its cells are under, its header, and how it aligns.

| Property | Type               | Description                                       |
| -------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `key`    | `string`           | The key each row's cell for this column is under. |
| `label`  | `string`           | The column's header.                              |
| `align?` | `'start' \| 'end'` | `end` for figures, so they line up.               |

### TableRow

One row of a kit `Table`: its cells by column key, its actions, and how to open it.

| Property   | Type                                  | Description                                        |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `key`      | `string`                              | The row's key, for React and for actions.          |
| `cells`    | `Readonly<Record<string, ReactNode>>` | The row's cells, by column key, already formatted. |
| `actions?` | `ReactNode`                           | Buttons for the row's actions.                     |
| `onOpen?`  | `() => void`                          | Opens the row's own page.                          |

### ValueProps

What a value renderer gets: the field and its value, and the currency for money.

Uses: [`Field`](core.md#field-type).

| Property    | Type      | Description                                   |
| ----------- | --------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `field`     | `Field`   | The field, with its type and meaning.         |
| `value`     | `unknown` | The stored value, such as an amount in cents. |
| `currency?` | `string`  | For money: the currency the value is in.      |

### ValueRenderers

Value renderers by type (`money`) or by reference target (`ref:customers`).

```ts
type ValueRenderers = Readonly<Record<string, ComponentType<ValueProps>>>;
```

Uses: [`ValueProps`](#valueprops).
